title: What If You Never Got Out of Bed for 60 Days? Space Agencies Pay to Find Out

scenes.text: What if you stayed in bed for 60 days straight? Space agencies pay volunteers to find out.
In these studies the bed is tilted six degrees head-down, so your blood drifts toward your head, the way it does in orbit.
Rule one: a shoulder stays on the mattress at all times. You eat, wash and use the toilet lying down.
Within weeks your legs start wasting. One volunteer's calf muscle was predicted to shrink by up to 25 percent.
Your hip bones lose two to four percent of their density, and the amount of blood your heart pumps per beat drops.
Then come two weeks of rehab and two years of check-ups. The bone comes back, slowly. Your body treats a bed like outer space.

description:
What if you never got out of bed for 60 days? NASA, ESA and the German Aerospace Center run exactly this experiment: volunteers lie for 60 to 70 days with the bed tilted six degrees head-down, keeping one shoulder on the mattress while eating, showering and using the toilet, because the fluid shift mimics weightlessness.
In the 2015 DLR study one volunteer was predicted to lose two to four percent of his hip bone density and up to 25 percent of his calf muscle; the heart pumps less blood per beat. Two weeks of rehab and two years of follow-up exams follow, and doctors say the bone loss is reversible but slow.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Half the volunteers in the 2015 study had to do jump training while lying flat, five or six times a week. Could you last 60 days? Drop your own what-if below.
